content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis not specified",
      "quote": "the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of PFS will only be reported in a descriptive manner.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that PFS will only be reported descriptively, but no specific descriptive analysis method (e.g., Kaplan-Meier estimates, medians, rates) is described for the primary endpoint in Section 9.3.2. The general time-to-event methods in 9.3.1 are mentioned, but the primary endpoint section lacks a clear analysis plan.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection under 9.3.2 detailing the descriptive analysis for PFS, including estimation methods, censoring rules, and presentation of results."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for primary endpoint",
      "quote": "PFS, defined as the time from randomization date to the first documented PD, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1 or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The endpoint definition lacks a clear specification of the estimand attributes: the population is implied but not explicitly stated, the intercurrent events (e.g., treatment switching, discontinuation) are not defined, and the summary measure (e.g., hazard ratio, median) is not specified in the endpoint definition.",
      "fix": "Provide a formal estimand framework for PFS, including the target population, variable definition, handling of intercurrent events (e.g., using treatment policy or hypothetical strategies), and the population-level summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "No analysis specified for ORR endpoint",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of participants with a CR or a PR on two consecutive occasions ≥4 weeks apart, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The ORR endpoint is listed as a key secondary endpoint, but no specific statistical analysis method is described for it in Section 9.3. The general categorical methods in 9.3.1 are mentioned, but there is no dedicated analysis section for ORR, including how the proportion and confidence intervals will be computed.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection for ORR analysis under 9.3, specifying the estimation method (e.g., Clopper-Pearson CI), comparison method (e.g., stratified CMH test), and handling of missing responses."
    },
    {
      "title": "No analysis specified for OS endpoint",
      "quote": "OS, defined as the time from randomization date to death due to any cause",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "OS is listed as a key secondary endpoint, but no specific analysis is described in Section 9.3. The general time-to-event methods are mentioned, but there is no dedicated OS analysis section, and it is unclear if OS will be analyzed descriptively or with formal testing.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection for OS analysis under 9.3, specifying the estimation method, censoring rules, and whether any formal comparison will be made."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for safety endpoints",
      "quote": "Incidence and severity of adverse events, with severity determined according to the NCI CTCAE v5.0",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "Safety endpoints (AEs, ECOG, vital signs, lab tests) are listed as secondary objectives, but no statistical analysis methods are described for them in Section 9.3. The general considerations mention descriptive statistics, but no specific safety analysis plan is provided.",
      "fix": "Add a safety analysis subsection detailing how AEs, ECOG changes, vital signs, and lab changes will be summarized and compared between treatment arms."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for DOR, CBR, and DCR endpoints",
      "quote": "DOR, defined as the time from the first occurrence of a documented objective response to disease progression or death from any cause (whichever occurs first), as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "DOR, CBR, and DCR are listed as additional secondary endpoints, but no specific analysis methods are described for them in Section 9.3. The general time-to-event and categorical methods are mentioned, but no dedicated sections exist for these endpoints.",
      "fix": "Add subsections for DOR, CBR, and DCR analyses, specifying estimation methods, censoring rules, and comparison methods."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistent handling of multiplicity",
      "quote": "No formal testing will be performed for neither the primary nor for the key secondary efficacy endpoints. Accordingly, a control for the overall type I error (α) applying a gate-keeping hierarchical sequential testing method will no longer be implemented.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that no formal testing will be performed, but Section 9.3.1 describes stratified log-rank tests and CMH tests for comparisons. This is inconsistent: if no formal testing is done, why are test methods described? Clarify whether these tests are only for descriptive p-values or if formal testing is still planned for some endpoints.",
      "fix": "Revise Section 9.3.1 to explicitly state that all tests are descriptive only, or remove the description of formal tests if they will not be performed."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inputs missing or inconsistent",
      "quote": "Originally, the sample size of this study was determined by the primary endpoint; therefore, the study was event driven.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2 Sample Size Determination",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size section does not provide the original assumptions (e.g., expected PFS hazard ratio, event rates, alpha, power) or the final sample size number. It only states that the study was event-driven and is now terminated. This is insufficient for a statistical review.",
      "fix": "Provide the original sample size calculation inputs (e.g., assumed HR, median PFS, alpha, power, number of events) and the final planned sample size, even if the study is terminated."
    }
  ]
}
